analyses.what_happens: i_rst_n_rd stays 0 for the whole trace, so the FIFO never enters use (both resets released) and ENV-01 (nnc_env.sv:51-53, active only when w_inuse = r_inuse | (i_rst_n_wr & i_rst_n_rd), line 45) never holds i_full_thr stable. i_rst_n_wr is released at the i_clk_wr rising edge in step 1 (ENV-05 is met). i_rst_n_sw=0 throughout, so the write block is on: o_full=1 and o_full_thr=(i_full_thr==0). The tool toggles i_full_thr 0->8->0->8 at steps 1/2/3. Step 2 is a falling edge of i_clk_wr, and i_rst_n_wr=1 there. At that step i_full_thr changes from 8 to 0, so o_full_thr changes from 0 to 1 between write edges. The negedge snapshot holds snap_wr=4'b0010 (o_full=1, o_full_thr=0, the value just after edge 1). At the next rising edge (step 3), {o_full,o_full_thr} just before the edge is 2'b11. snap_sw==i_rst_n_sw (0==0), so the term (snap_sw != i_rst_n_sw) || (snap_wr[1:0]=={o_full,o_full_thr}) is false and the assertion fails. The only cause of the change is the input change of i_full_thr. No pointer, flop or i_rst_n_sw changed. o_overflow and o_sw_rst_busy stay 0, so snap_wr[3:2] matches.
analyses.spec_says: spec/AsyncGrayFIFO_Design_Specification.md:270 (rules.json AF-6.2-06, line 2880): LVL-STS flag "changes after a clock edge (or after a synchronizer stage), never between edges except for the effect of the static thresholds". Spec :291: o_full_thr is a "Combinational function of i_full_thr and the pointers". Spec :273 (STATIC) and :418 (CDC-004): the thresholds are "written once, before the FIFO is used, and not changed while the FIFO is in use". The recorded designer decision is at rules.json:12782-12790, the question on AF-3-17: "'In use' = from the release of both hardware resets to the end of the test. The thresholds are set before the resets are released ...". Decision at rules.json:12827: "in use = after both hardware resets are released". Contract CHK-012 (contract.json:509) lists only i_clk_wr edges, i_rst_n_wr assertion and i_rst_n_sw changes as allowed change events. It leaves out the threshold exception that AF-6.2-06 states.
analyses.rtl_does: rtl/m_vlsit_afifo_wr.sv:102: w_wr_blk = reg_sw_rst_busy | ~i_rst_n_sw. Line 125: o_full = w_wr_blk | w_full_n. Line 126: o_full_thr = w_wr_blk ? (i_full_thr == '0) : (w_occ >= i_full_thr). o_full_thr follows i_full_thr combinationally, as the spec requires (:291, REQ-FUNC-018 AF-3-28). The top passes it straight through (m_vlsit_afifo_top.sv:90,95). o_overflow and o_sw_rst_busy are flops (wr.sv:158-163, 208-213, 224-225), so that part is consistent.
analyses.checker_does: nnc_chk_wr.sv:68-72 snapshots {o_overflow,o_sw_rst_busy,o_full,o_full_thr} and i_rst_n_sw at every negedge of i_clk_wr. Lines 115-117 require at the next posedge that o_full/o_full_thr are unchanged unless i_rst_n_sw changed. The hand fix comment is at line 114. Nothing excuses a change of i_full_thr, and the check is not limited to the in-use period in which i_full_thr is static.

candidates.evidence_for: The spec says explicitly that LVL-STS flags may change between edges through "the effect of the static thresholds" (spec:270, AF-6.2-06). The designer decision allows i_full_thr to change until both hardware resets are released (rules.json:12788, 12827), and that point is never reached here (i_rst_n_rd=0 throughout). The RTL matches the spec (wr.sv:126). The checker (nnc_chk_wr.sv:115-117) and the contract text (contract.json:509) leave out the threshold exception, so they flag legal behaviour.
candidates.evidence_against: The contract CHK-012 behavior, as written, does not list a threshold change as an allowed event. Following the contract text literally, the checker implements it faithfully, and the gap is in the contract rather than in the SVA coding.

candidates.evidence_for: AF-3-17 / CDC-004 (spec:273, :418) say the thresholds are written once before use. One could read 'use' as starting at the release of i_rst_n_wr for the write domain. ENV-01 would then need to hold i_full_thr stable from the first release of i_rst_n_wr, and this trace would be excluded.
candidates.evidence_against: The recorded designer decision (rules.json:12788, 12827) defines 'in use' as after both hardware resets are released, and ENV-01 (nnc_env.sv:45,51-53) implements exactly that. Strengthening it would contradict the decision unless the designer changes it.

candidates.evidence_for: The spec never defines 'before the FIFO is used' (the open questions at rules.json:12785 and 12824 say so). Whether a one-domain release counts as use was settled only by a delegated decision.
candidates.evidence_against: The decision exists and is unambiguous for this trace, so the spec gap is already closed for verification purposes.

candidates.evidence_for: o_full_thr does change between i_clk_wr edges.
candidates.evidence_against: The spec requires o_full_thr to be a combinational function of i_full_thr (spec:291, AF-3-28) and explicitly allows threshold-driven changes between edges (spec:270). The RTL has no defect here.

analyses.options: B: Add the AF-6.2-06 threshold exception to the CHK-012 contract text and to the checker. One way: also snapshot i_full_thr at the negedge (snap_thr), and accept a change of snap_wr[1:0] when snap_thr != i_full_thr. Another way: enforce the o_full/o_full_thr part only while the FIFO is in use (a checker copy of the env w_inuse: both resets released at least once). Keep the o_overflow/o_sw_rst_busy part unconditional. E (only if the designer revises the 'in use' decision at rules.json:12788 so that use starts at the i_rst_n_wr release): strengthen ENV-01 to hold i_full_thr stable once i_rst_n_wr has been released, citing AF-3-17 / AF-7.2-04 / AF-17.1.3-04. Do not do this without changing the decision. Secondary note: the failing edge (step 3) coincides with an assertion of i_rst_n_wr. Because of sampled-value semantics, disable iff does not mask it, but the between-edge change at step 2 is real regardless.

analyses.what_happens: i_full_thr=8 (=PARA_AFIFO_DEPTH), and both resets are released by step 2, so the FIFO is in use. One write is accepted at the i_clk_wr edge of step 3, which samples i_wr_en=1 at step 2. One read is accepted at the i_clk_rd edge of step 8, which samples i_rd_en=1 and o_empty=0 at step 7. After this the read pointer is 1. At step 8, i_rst_n_wr is asserted alone while i_rst_n_rd=1. It is released at the edge of step 9 (ENV-05 is met). This is a write-domain-only hardware reset after use. The write pointer and the write-side read-pointer synchronizer go to 0, but the read pointer stays at 1. ENV-03/ENV-07 block any further write: the write edges at 9, 11, 13 sample i_wr_en=0. The synchronizer re-acquires rgray=1, so by step 13 w_rbin_s=1. i_rst_n_rd is then asserted alone at step 11 with no overlap, which resets the read pointer but reaches the write side only after S edges. Now w_occ = reg_wbin - w_rbin_s = 0 - 1 = 4'hF (>= 8), so o_full_thr=1. The Gray compare (wgray=0 vs rgray_s^4'b1100) is false, so o_full=0. With i_rst_n_sw=1 and o_sw_rst_busy=0, clause (c) requires o_full_thr == full_clean == 0, and the check fails at the write edge of step 13 (or step 15 with sampled values of step 14). The trace shows o_full_thr=1, o_full=0 at steps 13-14.
analyses.spec_says: spec:424 / rules.json AF-7.2-12 (line 4113): "If only one domain is reset after the FIFO was used, the pointer state of the two domains becomes inconsistent. The IP neither detects nor repairs this (ASM-005)." spec:1099 / AF-12-07 (rules.json:7813): ERR-003 "Reset asserted in one domain only, after the FIFO was used; ... FIFO state inconsistent; not detected; ... Clear/recovery: Reset both domains; ... Integrator responsibility (ASM-005)". spec:1461 ASM-005 says operation starts only after both domains have left reset, and the inconsistency is a "Consequence, not a requirement". spec:424 / AF-7.2-11 / DEC-009 (spec:1476): the two resets are independent and "need not be asserted together". Contract CHK-023 (contract.json:757-758) deliberately stimulates a one-domain reset and says "The handshake after a one-domain reset is not checked. After both domains are reset, the FIFO works normally." Contract CHK-013 (contract.json:524) says "At every rising edge of i_clk_wr with i_rst_n_wr=1", with no exclusion of the inconsistent state.
analyses.rtl_does: rtl/m_vlsit_afifo_wr.sv:141-146 and :149-154: reg_wbin/reg_wgray are reset to 0 by i_rst_n_wr only. Lines 232-242: the read-Gray synchronizer is reset by i_rst_n_wr and then resamples the live read pointer. Line 120: w_occ = reg_wbin - w_rbin_s (modulo 16). Line 106: w_full_n is a Gray equality compare. Lines 125-126: o_full and o_full_thr. When the pointers are consistent, w_occ==8 iff w_full_n, so clause (c) holds. After the write-only reset, the pointers are inconsistent (wbin=0 < rbin=1), w_occ wraps to 15, and o_full_thr=1 while o_full=0. This is exactly the undetected inconsistency that the spec describes.
analyses.checker_does: nnc_chk_wr.sv:122: full_clean = o_full && i_rst_n_sw && !o_sw_rst_busy. Lines 123-127 check clauses (a)-(d) at every write edge, with only disable iff (!i_rst_n_wr). The checker has an exclusion for one-domain resets only for CHK-011 and only for a read-only reset (rd_only_rst, lines 76-79, used at line 107). There is no exclusion for a write-only reset and none for CHK-013, so the check stays active in the state that the spec calls inconsistent and undefined.

candidates.evidence_for: The spec explicitly says that after a one-domain reset following use, the pointer state is inconsistent and the IP neither detects nor repairs it (spec:424, :1099, :1461; AF-7.2-12, AF-12-07). Clause (c) relies on consistent pointers (occupancy 8 <=> full), so it cannot hold in that state. The env (nnc_env.sv:90-109) already models this window as legal (w_rst_pend) and only stops traffic. The checker already has a hand fix of the same kind for CHK-011 (nnc_chk_wr.sv:74-79), but that fix covers only a read-only reset and only CHK-011.
candidates.evidence_against: Contract CHK-013 (contract.json:524) states no such exclusion, and the CHK-023 exclusion (contract.json:758) names only the handshake. Following the contract literally, the checker is faithful and the contract needs the extension.

candidates.evidence_for: The spec says the state is 'inconsistent' but does not say which output properties remain guaranteed in that state. The contract limits the CHK-023 exclusion to 'the handshake', so it is unclear whether the threshold/full consistency checks are also void until both domains are reset together.
candidates.evidence_against: "Inconsistent ... neither detects nor repairs" plus "Clear/recovery: Reset both domains" (ERR-003) clearly makes pointer-derived flag relations undefined until a joint reset.

candidates.evidence_for: ERR-003 / ASM-005 label recovery as 'Integrator responsibility'. One could read this as an obligation never to reset one domain alone after use. ENV-07/08 would then become an assumption that resets overlap.
candidates.evidence_against: The spec calls the one-domain reset a consequence, not a requirement (ASM-005, spec:1461). It says the resets "need not be asserted together" (DEC-009, AF-7.2-11), and the contract's own CHK-023 stimulus applies one-domain resets as legal input. The env header (nnc_env.sv:37-38) and ENV-07/08 deliberately leave this free. Forbidding it would be an assumption the spec does not support.

candidates.evidence_for: o_full_thr=1 while o_full=0 with i_full_thr=DEPTH, which breaks the literal clause (c).
candidates.evidence_against: It happens only after a write-only hardware reset after use, which the spec defines as an inconsistent, unrepaired state (AF-7.2-12, ERR-003). In every consistent state the RTL equations (wr.sv:106,120,126) satisfy (c).

analyses.options: B: Extend the contract CHK-013 text (and the CHK-023 exclusion) so that the pointer-derived flag relations are not checked after a one-domain hardware reset until both domains have been reset with overlapping windows and released. In nnc_chk_wr.sv, replace or generalize rd_only_rst (lines 76-79) with a checker copy of the env's reset-pairing state (r_dirty/r_ovl/w_rst_pend, nnc_env.sv:90-104), so that it covers write-only and read-only resets, plus a 'used' flag. Apply it as an extra disable to a_CHK_013 clauses (c)/(d) and to the other occupancy-dependent checks (CHK-006, and CHK-003 on the read side if affected). Clauses (a) and (b) do not depend on pointer consistency and could stay unconditional. C: If the designer considers that flag relations must hold even in the inconsistent state, the spec must say so. That would then turn this into an RTL issue, but nothing in the spec currently requires it. Do not add an env assumption that forbids one-domain resets: the spec (DEC-009, ASM-005, CHK-023) treats them as legal input.
